title: NEB-Style Questions — Physical Quantities & Dimensions
notes:
Q1. (Short answer) Distinguish between precision and accuracy.
Ans: Precision is reproducibility of repeated measurements (low scatter); accuracy is closeness to the true value. A reading can be precise but not accurate (systematic error).

Q2. (Short answer) State the principle of homogeneity of dimensions and its one use.
Ans: Dimensions of every term in a physical equation must be the same; used to check the dimensional correctness of relations.

Q3. (Derivation) Using dimensional analysis derive the relation for the period T of a simple pendulum.
Ans: Assume T = k lᵃ gᵇ; [T] = [L]ᵃ[L T⁻²]ᵇ ⇒ −2b = 1 ⇒ b = −½, a = ½; T = k√(l/g) with k = 2π.

Q4. (Numerical) Convert 5 joules into erg.
Ans: 1 J = 10⁷ erg, so 5 J = 5 × 10⁷ erg (using n₁u₁ = n₂u₂ with [M L² T⁻²]).

Q5. (Concept) Why can dimensional analysis not distinguish work and torque?
Ans: Both have dimensions [M L² T⁻²]; dimensional analysis compares only dimensions, so quantities differing in physical nature but sharing dimensions cannot be told apart.

Q6. (Liquidity) A measurement gives 0.0002040 s. How many significant figures? Express in scientific notation.
Ans: 4 sig figs (0.0002040 → trailing zero counts); = 2.040 × 10⁻⁴ s.

Q7. (Concept) What do you mean by the order of magnitude of a quantity? Give an example.
Ans: The nearest power of ten of the value. The radius of Earth (6.4 × 10⁶ m) has order of magnitude 10⁶ m.
